newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo reports profit, beating expectations of loss.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo reports profit, beating expectations of loss.

text.p: Internet media and search company Yahoo Inc. said Tuesday it posted a modest profit, beating Wall Street's expectations of a fourth quarter loss.
The company reported a profit of $96,000 vs. a profit of $92,000 a year earlier and much improved from a loss of $1.15 million in the 1996 third quarter.
Revenues were $8.55 million vs. $1.075 million a year earlier and up 55 percent from the third quarter of 1996.
Wall Street had expected the company to turn in a loss, with consensus estimates at 5 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
The company reported revenues of $19.1 million and a net loss of $2.3 million for the full year.
Yahoo! Chief Financial Officer Gary Valenzuela said total page views including Yahoo! Japan rose to 20 million a day in the month of December.
That was up from over 15 million a day in September, including Yahoo! Japan, which amounted to about a million page views per day in September and 1.4 million in December.

"We're going to emphasise growth," Valenzuela said in an interview. "We're focused on building long-term value for shareholders, particularly at this early stage, growing market share and building out the Yahoo! family of properties."
Yahoo!'s advertiser base increased to 550 in the fourth quarter, up from 340 in the third quarter, adding a combination of consumer brands and technology companies.
